page: Google Cloud Platform t2a-standard-16 is a general-purpose server instance powered by the ARMv8 architecture. It features 16 dedicated physical cores utilizing the Ampere Neoverse-N1 processor running at 3.0 GHz, with a single thread per core. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware.

Performance benchmarks place this instance in the middle tier for most multi-core and memory operations. The stress-ng multi-core CPU score is 28983.31, and the Geekbench multi-core score is 9311.0, both aligning with average tier performance. However, single-core capabilities represent a notable tradeoff, with Geekbench single-core scores of 1078.0 and bzip3 single-threaded decompression at 8.61 GB/sec falling into the bottom 25% of tested servers. Cryptographic performance is also weak, as evidenced by a PassMark CPU encryption score of 2588.14, likely due to the lack of specialized instruction sets like AVX or SHA extensions.

The ARM-based architecture provides a cost-efficient hardware profile for scale-out workloads, offering high physical core density without hyperthreading overhead. Memory bandwidth is robust, reaching 1129.87 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 129.41 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. Static web serving throughput reaches 18.26 GB/sec, and Redis SET operations perform at 21.18 million operations per second. These metrics indicate the instance is suited for multi-threaded applications, static web serving, database operations, and software compilation, while it is less efficient for single-threaded tasks or heavy cryptographic workloads.
